subject: reading
title: The Garden Storm
about: Bert and Gran are planting the garden when a storm rolls in, and the drops turn out to be just what the plants needed. The story practises er, ar and or (Bert, her, garden, carrots, dark, storm, porch, thunder), two-syllable words and the endings -ing, -ed and -ness (splashing, booming, harmed, helped, darkness), with the day names Saturday and Sunday. It is decodable at CKLA Unit 4, which the class usually reaches in January to February.
tip: Ask him to find every word with an -ing, -ed or -ness ending and say the base word underneath: harm in harmed, dark in darkness.

passage.text:
It is Saturday.
Bert helps Gran in her garden.
Gran plants corn and carrots.
Bert digs in the soil.

Then dark clouds drift in.
The wind picks up.
"A storm!" says Gran.
Drops are splashing on the garden.
Thunder is booming.
Bert and Gran rush to the porch.
They are safe and snug.

After the storm, the darkness lifts.
The plants are wet but not harmed.
"The storm helped us!" says Bert.
"The garden got lots of drops."
Gran grins.
"On Sunday we will check for sprouts."

cards.q: Who helps Gran in her garden?
cards.note: The second line says Bert helps Gran.
Gran plants corn and carrots while Bert digs in the soil.

cards.q: Where do Bert and Gran rush to?
cards.note: They rush to the porch when the storm hits.

cards.q: What is booming in the storm?
cards.note: Thunder is booming while the drops splash on the garden.

cards.q: What happens first in the story?
cards.note: Planting comes first; the storm comes after the dark clouds drift in.

cards.q: At the end, what will they check for on Sunday?
cards.note: Gran says they will check for sprouts on Sunday.

cards.q: How do Bert and Gran feel on the porch?
cards.note: The story says they are safe and snug on the porch.

cards.q: What is the lesson of the story?
cards.note: Bert sees that the drops helped the garden, so a storm can be a good thing.
Sprouts are the first little plants that pop up from seeds.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Storm, stork and stem look alike; only storm is in the story.
